title: Milton Mezzrow's friendship and recordings
summary: Price describes Mezz's friendship, helping each other, and records he made.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah...we didn't talk about Mezz and all...

Well, Milton and I became friends, very close friends, when he came home from being away in the '40s. And I knew... we knew a lot of people. And Mezz and I had the concerts in Philadelphia, but I never judge a man by his skin or by...oh, he was once a prisoner, or, you know. As long as he treat me all right and / courteous to my friends, I accept him. So I gave Mezz every cent in Philadelphia...we made fifty bucks. That was enough to tide him over. In Philadelphia he played at the Academy of Music and when we became good friends sometimes I would stay in Philadelphia and he would meet the musicians at the station, here in New York, at Penn Station, with the tickets. And, you know what I mean, sort of act like a group leader, and bring them over.
So now Mezz and I became friends and he reciprocated--he found an angel who had money and he let me make those records

that /I made with Cousin Joe and Socks Wilson, and Coot Grant and Hot Lips Page, and then I made a series of things, "Step Down, Step Up," and "133" and all that. He reciprocated. And then in '48 when we went to the festival and Willie 'the Lion' didn't go, I went with him. So we became very, very close. But, as I said, those guys always would, in the end, not try to do anything to you, but try to make you make mistakes. And so, for that reason...but we never fell out.
